text:
The occurrence of generalized convulsions, associated with signs of pre-
eclampsia during pregnancy, labour, or within 42 days of delivery. Referred to
as atypical eclampsia if it occurs in the absence of high blood pressure and after
7 days post-partum.
Incidence is widely variable. Worldwide range reported to be 1 in 100 - 1 in
3,448 pregnancies in Nigeria, it is commoner among un-booked patients.
Aetiology
Not exactly known; Its precursor is pre-eclampsia. A disease of primigravidae
or multigravidae with pregnancy for a new consort.
